lead.headline: U.S. destroys five Iranian tankers; Iran fires missiles at Jordan base
lead.dek: Jordan says it intercepted 18 of 20 ballistic missiles; Brent crude touched $99 a barrel
body: U.S. forces destroyed five Iranian crude tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island on Tuesday, and Iran's Revolutionary Guard answered overnight with ballistic missiles aimed at the Al Azraq air base in Jordan and two U.S. Navy destroyers, U.S. Central Command and Iranian state media said.

CENTCOM said the strikes on the Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, Riesco and Derya came after the Guard fired missiles at a Navy warship twice in 48 hours; the ship evaded both, and crews were told to abandon the tankers before they were hit. Jordan's armed forces said they engaged 20 missiles and destroyed 18, with two falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties reported.

The Guard said its missiles caused "significant damage" to the destroyers; a U.S. official told NBC News the response was ineffective. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran will "lose tankers" each time it fires on U.S. ships. Brent crude touched $99 a barrel Tuesday and Al Jazeera reported it at $99.49 early Wednesday, six months into the war.

briefs.headline: Hurricane Lowell leaves 33,000 without power on Kauai
briefs.summary: KIUC said 90% of its members lost power Tuesday and 1,500 miles of line need inspection; it aims to finish transmission repairs in two days and distribution circuits by week's end.

briefs.headline: Sununu and Pappas win New Hampshire Senate primaries
briefs.summary: Former Sen. John Sununu beat Scott Brown for the Republican nomination and Rep. Chris Pappas beat Karishma Manzur for the Democratic one Tuesday, setting up the November race for retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen's seat.

briefs.headline: Kavanaugh rejects Missouri bid to use new congressional map
briefs.summary: Justice Brett Kavanaugh on Tuesday denied Missouri's request to pause a Sept. 3 state Supreme Court ruling that struck the map, drawn to give Republicans 7 of 8 House seats; the 2022 map stands for November.

briefs.headline: NTSB finds no sign Miami jet's speed brakes or reversers deployed
briefs.summary: Flight data show the Boeing 767 touched down at 158 knots and brakes were applied, then released at 120 knots as throttles rose to go-around thrust, the NTSB said Tuesday; the two pilots are to be interviewed Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Israel orders U.K. consulate closed after settlement trade ban
briefs.summary: Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said Britain's East Jerusalem consulate must close within 30 days and 12 Britons, including Jeremy Corbyn, are barred, after Britain, France and Canada announced bans on settlement goods Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Kyiv's toll from Tuesday's Russian strikes rises to five
briefs.summary: Mayor Vitali Klitschko said five people were killed and 23 injured, 14 of them hospitalized, in the missile and drone attack that ended Moscow's three-day pause, up from two dead reported Tuesday morning. Blasts began about 3:30 a.m.

briefs.headline: Kenya rights body warns Ruto's foreign-trader crackdown risks abuses
briefs.summary: Enforcement of President William Ruto's order to close small businesses run by foreigners began Monday. KNCHR chair Claris Ogangah cited complaints of threats and intimidation; the government has opened a 90-day registration window.

briefs.headline: Indonesia's fires lead the world in emissions, Copernicus data show
briefs.summary: Fires on peatland and forest in Kalimantan and Sumatra emitted 19.7 million metric tons Sept. 1-7, more than a third of the global total and 273% above the seasonal average, according to Fire Emissions Watch, built on EU Copernicus data.

briefs.headline: Justices hear jail-death appeals as state seeks to bar neglect claims
briefs.summary: The Supreme Court heard two deliberate-indifference appeals Tuesday. The state argued families of inmates who die in custody cannot seek damages from it and must sue officers; a ruling could take months, attorney Jesse Forbes said.

briefs.headline: Parkersburg council passes $3 recycling charge, PFAS financing
briefs.summary: Council voted 6-3 Tuesday to charge every resident $3 a month for recycling to comply with a July ruling by Judge J.D. Beane, and unanimously approved financing for the Utility Board's $25.7M forever-chemical filtration project.

briefs.headline: Morrisey signs MOU for federal nuclear campus bid
briefs.summary: West Virginia became the sixth state to sign an Energy Department memorandum on Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses, after Idaho, Tennessee, Utah, Oklahoma and Louisiana; Morrisey called it a chance to "help lead America's nuclear renaissance."

briefs.headline: Pack vows to defend Hope Scholarship against Mingo parents' suit
briefs.summary: Treasurer Larry Pack said he will 'aggressively oppose' any attempt to reverse universal expansion after Mingo County parents sued Friday in Kanawha Circuit Court. The program has $297M in this year's budget and 26,617 applicants.

regional.item: Point Pleasant council voted down a downtown outdoor-drinking district Tuesday that would have covered Main Street from First to Sixth streets.
St. Albans council approved placing a VFW-owned World War II howitzer at Roadside Park on Tuesday, near the Rosie the Riveter display.
Wood County's school board voted 3-2 Tuesday to delay the scaled-back Parkersburg High stadium plan eight weeks so backers can seek more money.

away.item: A Springfield, Mass., man who ran a Bennington County cocaine and fentanyl ring was sentenced Tuesday in Rutland federal court to 12 years.

hotspots.item: WSAZ on Tuesday identified the two killed in Saturday's UTV crash on Bergoo Road as Maggie Driggs, 24, of the Charleston area, and Richard Chandler, 43, of Hurricane.
The Army Corps on Tuesday opened comment through Oct. 19 on its draft study of North Topsail Beach's inlet and beach plan, with a hearing Sept. 22 at 6 p.m. at Town Hall.

briefs.headline: Yu launches re-election bid as eight seek Prince George mayoralty
briefs.summary: Mayor Simon Yu opened his campaign Tuesday, pledging to meet 100 employers and investors in his first year and back a detox-and-rehab navigation centre pilot. The city lists eight mayoral candidates; nominations close Friday at 4 p.m.

briefs.headline: Two Cariboo residents fined $5,750 for night hunting of mule deer
briefs.summary: Each paid a $2,500 fine and a $375 surcharge in Williams Lake Provincial Court after pleading guilty under the Wildlife Act to killing a buck in a private field after 10:40 p.m. on Oct. 8, 2022, the Conservation Officer Service said.

briefs.headline: Sto:lo Collective to demolish former St. Mary's residential school
briefs.summary: The Mission site, B.C.'s longest-running residential school at 121 years, comes down in 2027 and an interpretive centre opens in 2028, the 21-community collective said Tuesday. A 2021 investigation found 158 child deaths tied to the school.

briefs.headline: Eby unveils border signs as B.C. backs Ottawa's countertariffs
briefs.summary: The premier said Tuesday in Victoria that new signs at B.C. crossings will read "strong, proud and will never be the 51st state. Sorry!" He kept the ban on U.S. alcohol in provincial liquor stores and said more countermeasures are possible.

briefs.headline: Trump orders bans on Canadian alcohol, dairy, motorcycles from Sept. 29
briefs.summary: Trump signed five orders Tuesday barring most Canadian alcohol, whey, molasses and motorcycles from Sept. 29 and pulling Canadian goods from U.S. procurement lists he put at $50 billion a year. Ottawa is assessing them, LeBlanc said.

briefs.headline: China discloses defence talks with Canadian officials
briefs.summary: China's defence ministry said a Sept. 4 meeting was the countries' fifth defence coordination dialogue and the first in eight years; Canada's Defence Department confirmed it. Pierre Poilievre said Canadians learned of it from Chinese media.

briefs.headline: Hubble and Webb find tiny objects beyond Neptune keep old colors
briefs.summary: NASA said Tuesday Hubble and Webb observed 27 newly found trans-Neptunian objects, the smallest about 3 miles across, and that even the smallest keep surface colors recording their history. Two papers are in The Astronomical Journal.

briefs.headline: Extreme heat rises fastest in the north-central Amazon, study finds
briefs.summary: A Lancaster University-led study finds dry-season extreme temperatures in 10% of the Amazon basin, more than 700,000 square kilometers, rose at least 0.75 degrees Celsius a decade since 1981, in a region away from the deforestation zones.

briefs.headline: Chesapeake Bay underwater grasses grow 7% to 89,385 acres
briefs.summary: The Virginia Institute of Marine Science's 2025 survey mapped 89,385 acres of underwater grasses in the bay and its tidal rivers, up 6,134 acres from 2024 and the most since 2018, with the gains in saltier water.

briefs.headline: GPS collars show male lions chase hyenas, not the reverse
briefs.summary: A University of KwaZulu-Natal-led study in Frontiers in Ethology tracked 17 lions and 14 spotted hyenas over four years in Namibia and Botswana and found lions, especially males, moved toward hyenas while hyenas mostly moved away.

briefs.headline: NSA, FBI and CISA accuse six Chinese AI firms of model distillation
briefs.summary: A joint advisory issued Tuesday says DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun and Z.AI extracted billions of tokens from U.S. frontier models in distillation campaigns the agencies call the core of their development strategy.

briefs.headline: OpenAI claims Navier-Stokes proof; NYU mathematician alleges misconduct
briefs.summary: OpenAI said Tuesday an unreleased model proved the Navier-Stokes equations can blow up, checked in Lean. NYU's Tristan Buckmaster says OpenAI took his approach after learning of unpublished work; Sebastien Bubeck of OpenAI denies it.

briefs.headline: AI weather model mistimes D-Day storm's clearing, Reading study finds
briefs.summary: University of Reading researchers ran 50 AI forecasts for June 5-6, 1944, against 1944 records; the model placed June 5's storm but mistimed its clearing and gave June 6 a 30% chance of winds too strong for landing craft.
